params.body:
gentells.com's Generation filter offered only Gen Z. The filter lists only generations a published post carries, and of 78 posts 22 carried one (all Gen Z, guessed from word counts at import) and 56 none. The posts were read for who they are about, by the Gentells Standard's cohort rules, and the result is reviewed separately; this applies it as a run on the box.

## Change

`bin/retag-posts.mjs <plan.json> [--run=<name>] [--dry]` and `--undo=<run>`. The plan: `[{id, generations, lifestages, why}]`.
- Only the Standard's terms that may be tagged (Gen Beta is reserved), Tweens together with Kids (a subgroup is never tagged alone), ZAlpha together with a macro generation (a micro generation is a lens over a border). A plan that breaks one of these is refused whole, before anything is written.
- Only live posts, and only `generation_tags` and `lifestage_tags`: topics and regions stay.
- `article_retag_undo` keeps the tags before; `--undo` puts them back. updated_at moves, so the site fetches each post again.
- The output lists every change and the count per generation after the run.

## Checks

- `test/retag-posts.test.mjs` (2): refusals (Tweens alone, ZAlpha alone, Gen Beta, a draft) write nothing; a dry run writes nothing; a run sets only the cohort fields; undo restores them.
- Full suite 1221/1227; the 6 are `report-render` (`pdftoppm`, installed on the box).
- Dry run on a copy of production with the reviewed plan: 32 of 78 posts change; afterwards Gen Z 18, ZAlpha 1, Gen Alpha 11, so the filter offers all three.

Nothing runs at deploy. The plan file is handed over separately after review.
params.title: Set the generation and lifestage of live posts from a reviewed plan
